name: Small Business Video Ideas
blurb: 45 small business video ideas for shops, cafes and makers, each with a hook and format
title: 45 Small Business Video Ideas (With Hooks and Formats)
description: 45 content ideas for small businesses: behind the scenes, product demos, customer stories and sketches, each with a 2-second hook and format. Phone only.
h1: 45 Small Business Video Ideas, Each With a Hook
answer: This list is for owners of shops, cafes, studios and online stores who want to make short videos about their business with one phone. Each idea says what to film, the hook for the first two seconds and the format, so you can plan a few weeks of posts in one sitting.

items.d: Film keys, lights, the first coffee and the sign flipping. Hook: the key turning in the lock. Format: POV montage.
Show one order being wrapped and labelled, hiding the customer's details. Hook: the empty box. Format: hands only.
Show each step in a few seconds. Hook: the finished product first. Format: process timelapse.
One clip per hour of your real day. Hook: the alarm time. Format: vlog.

items.t: The mistake that taught us something
items.d: Share a harmless early mistake and what changed. Hook: the bad first version. Format: talking head.

items.t: Receiving a new delivery of stock
items.d: Unbox new stock and react. Hook: the boxes stacked at the door. Format: hands and voice-over.
The calm end of the day sped up. Hook: the last customer leaving, filmed only with permission. Format: timelapse.
Introduce each person with one line, only with their agreement. Hook: everyone saying their job at once. Format: quick cuts.
Compare the first set-up with today. Hook: the old photo. Format: before and after.

items.t: Three ways to use one product
items.d: Show three real uses of a best seller. Hook: the product held up with the number 3. Format: hands only.
Pick a common question and answer it in one clip. Hook: the question on screen. Format: talking head.
Slow, detailed shots of texture and sound. Hook: the most satisfying detail. Format: ASMR style.

items.t: How to choose the right size or option
items.d: A short guide that saves customers confusion. Hook: two options side by side. Format: explainer.
For services like repairs or cleaning, show a real result with the customer's permission. Hook: the before shot. Format: before and after.
Show the newest item or menu change. Hook: the reveal from under a cloth. Format: reveal.
Put a product through a fair, safe test, like a bag carrying books. Hook: the test set-up. Format: experiment.
Show how to look after something you sell. Hook: a damaged example next to a cared-for one. Format: tutorial.
Put together a bundle for an occasion. Hook: the finished box. Format: hands only.

items.t: Why a regular keeps coming back
items.d: Short interview with a happy customer who agreed to appear. Hook: their first line. Format: interview.
Read a real review and thank the person. Hook: the review on screen. Format: talking head.
Recommend a nearby business or park. Hook: walking out of your door toward it. Format: POV.
A weekly series answering one question. Hook: the question card. Format: series.

items.t: How we support a local cause
items.d: Show something you do for the neighbourhood, without overstating it. Hook: the activity in action. Format: vlog.
Show a tool or ingredient up close and reveal it. Hook: the extreme close-up. Format: game.

items.t: Show the people who supply you
items.d: Visit a supplier who agreed to be filmed. Hook: their workshop or farm. Format: mini documentary.
Tell the story of your very first sale. Hook: the first receipt or photo. Format: storytime.
A simple thanks with something handmade. Hook: a note written in close-up. Format: talking head.
Share a skill a professional in your field knows. Hook: a common mistake on screen. Format: tutorial.
Correct one belief people have, without making claims you cannot back up. Hook: the myth in big text. Format: talking head.

items.d: Three short lessons. Hook: the first lesson. Format: talking head.
Show what goes into making one item, without exact figures if you prefer. Hook: the item next to its materials. Format: explainer.

items.t: A tool I could not work without
items.d: Show it and why it matters. Hook: the tool in your hand. Format: hands only.
Advice linked to the time of year, such as care in rainy weather. Hook: the weather outside. Format: tips.
Show a real habit, like reusing boxes. Hook: the pile of boxes. Format: vlog.

items.d: The one question every customer asks. Hook: several clips of people asking it, or a caption. Format: talking head.
Play a seller who cannot stop telling the plain truth about products. Hook: Honestly, you do not need this. Format: sketch.
A comic story about two customers' orders swapped. Hook: the wrong name on the bag. Format: sketch.
Play every type of coworker a new hire meets on day one, all yourself. Hook: Welcome, we're like a family here. Format: POV sketch.

sections.h: How to pick and film a small business video
body: Pick ideas that show what makes your business yours: the people, the craft and the details customers never see. Batch-film a few on a quiet day so posting never depends on finding time later.

ol: Choose three ideas from different groups so your feed has variety.
Film vertically in the best light in your space, and tidy the frame before you record.
Get permission from staff, customers and suppliers before they appear, and hide personal details.
Cut each video to 15 to 60 seconds with captions and one clear ending, such as where to find you.
Post on a rhythm you can keep through busy weeks, and repeat the formats your customers respond to.

body.note: Make only claims you can back up, and use music you have the rights to or the platform's library.

ul: Open on the finished product, then show how it was made.
Start with a customer question in big text.
Show the messiest moment of the process first.
Begin with a sound: the key in the lock, the tape gun, the grinder.
Lead with a mistake or myth and correct it.
Put a surprising close-up on screen and ask what it is.
Start with a time stamp: 6am, before we open.

faq.q: Can I use the linked sketches to promote my business?
faq.a: Yes. The scripts are original and licensed CC BY 4.0, so you can adapt them for commercial accounts. Credit Script: cv.cm in the caption or description.

faq.q: I am not comfortable on camera. What can I film?
faq.a: Process shots, packing videos, product close-ups and voice-over tips need no face. A team member who enjoys it can also front the talking-head ideas.

faq.q: How do I film customers properly?
faq.a: Ask first, explain where the video will be posted, and keep anyone who says no out of frame. Never show order labels, addresses or screens with personal data.
